headline: NQ extends to a new Globex high after the record Nasdaq-100 close, but overnight pullbacks still hold
body: Nasdaq-100 futures trade at 31,380.25, up 62.50 points (+0.20%), after printing a new Globex high at 31,410.75 and easing roughly 30 points from it. The overnight range has widened from 59.75 to 85.25 points, which is still only about 0.27% of index value, and the retracement from the high is the decisive observation: range expansion without a failed pullback is not evidence of mean-reversion failure. The cash index closed on 5 October at a record 31,076.44, up 0.87%, with a record intraday high of 31,117.36, led by Nvidia reaching an all-time high and Taiwan Semiconductor trading at intraday records. Asia has handed over constructively rather than aggressively: the Nikkei 225 is up 0.59% at 70,361.23 near its session high of 70,375.02 and the ASX 200 is up 0.56% at 8,735.30, while E-mini S&P 500 futures add only 0.11%, so equity-futures leadership is narrow. Cross-asset alignment remains incomplete, which is what holds Tail in the low band: the 10-year Treasury yield sits at 5.31% near its highest level since 2002, the 2-year was 4.83% at the latest H.15 observation, Brent crude remains above $100 with WTI at $89.59, and VIX is compressed at 15.52. Equities advancing against rising yields and firm energy is a conflict, and conflicting signals raise Stress rather than Tail. Stress therefore stays elevated at 46%, reflecting the yield backdrop, elevated crude, Middle East tensions and record-bullish sell-side positioning with 60% of S&P 500 stocks carrying Buy ratings. Confidence is high at 86% on verified current futures, index, volatility, yield, energy and Asian cash levels together with a verified seven-day U.S. calendar; the shared Finviz context file was stale and only partially collected on this run and was therefore not used. The forecast reaches WATCH only for the two hours spanning the Williams speech, the U.S. cash open and the Bowman speech, where an aligned bullish regime entering a record-high open is the configuration most capable of producing opening-auction continuation. That continuation is a scenario, not an observation.

lookbackSummary: The prior 24 hours of published Claude assessments stayed in the low Tail band except the 19:00 UTC hour, which reached WATCH at 20% during the U.S. afternoon advance. Tail ran from 15% early in the Asian session on 5 October down to 6% by 08:00 UTC, climbed through the European and U.S. sessions to a 20% peak at 19:00 UTC as the cash index pushed to its record, then decayed steadily to 9% by 00:00 UTC. Stress fell throughout, from 62% to 45%, as realised volatility compressed even while yields stayed high. The 06:00 UTC hour has no published assessment and is recorded as unavailable rather than reconstructed.
outlookSummary: The published path keeps Tail in the low band for 22 of the 24 forecast hours and reaches WATCH only at 13:00 and 14:00 UTC, which span the Williams speech, the U.S. cash open and the Bowman speech. Tail eases to 10% through the thin late-Asian hours, steps up from the European cash open at 08:00 UTC, peaks at 21% at the U.S. open, then decays through the afternoon with a secondary 17% reading in the power hour into the 20:00 UTC cash close. Stress tracks the same shape between 44% and 55%. Confidence declines from 86% to 78% across the window as distance from the verified overnight price evidence grows. Every hour beyond the current clock hour is conditional: no European or U.S. price path is observed at the assessment cutoff.
